newsitem.title: JORDAN: King, Arafat insist Israel must adhere to accords.
newsitem.headline: King, Arafat insist Israel must adhere to accords.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat insisted in crisis talks that Israel must honour its peace deals with the Palestinians despite last week's suicide bombings in Jerusalem, officials said on Tuesday.
They said the two leaders however expressed concern that the Jewish state was exploiting the latest bombings to backtrack on peace commitments.

"They both stressed the importance of commitment to agreements signed between the two sides -- the Palestinian and Israeli -- and not to empty them of their content or ignoring what has been attained so far," a senior Jordanian official told Reuters.
Both Jordan and the PLO have been in agreement that Israel has been footdragging on implementing a 1993 interim peace.

Officials said the king supported Arafat's view that the bombings which left 15 people killed, including the two Arab bombers, were being used as a pretext by Israel to retract from signed peace deals with the Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was quoted on Sunday as saying that Israel would not honour peace deals it signed with Arafat unless the Palestinian president cracked down on Islamic radicals.
Arafat, who arrived in Jordan on Monday, is expected to hold talks with Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali at noon.
King Hussein has said the bombings could have been precipitated by growing frustrations with a stalled peace process and anger over an accelerated Jewish settlement drive in the West Bank.
He has expressed increasing exasperation with Netanyahu's policies, publicly doubting his resolve to advance the peace process.

Jordan is worried by the repercussions of renewed violence in Palestinian territories on its own stability. The kingdom's 4.2 million people have close ethnic ties with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
